findings.summary: F2 stages the wrong markdown path for the ledger pair
findings.description: Critical: F2 says Step 11.5 runs `git add openspec/changes/$CHANGE_ID/choices.json choices.md`; the second path is repository-root `choices.md`, not `openspec/changes/$CHANGE_ID/choices.md`, so implementing the plan literally can commit only half of the ledger pair.
findings.recommendation: Change the planned command to stage both full paths, e.g. `git add "openspec/changes/$CHANGE_ID/choices.json" "openspec/changes/$CHANGE_ID/choices.md"`, and make task 3.7 assert both ledger paths are named in the hook.
findings.resolution: Correct F2's command and extend the workflow-hook content test so the regression is pinned before implementation.

findings.summary: The no-diff re-audit commit policy is incompatible with the existing ledger writer
findings.description: Critical: F2 claims a no-diff re-audit commits nothing, but `run_audit.py` creates a fresh header each run (`generated_at` and `run_id`) and `choices_ledger.write_ledger()` always rewrites `choices.json`, with `choices.md` rendering the generated timestamp. Task 3.6 only checks stable IDs and count, so the plan does not verify the commit-skipping behavior it relies on.
findings.recommendation: Either remove the no-diff commit claim, or add an explicit implementation/test plan that detects semantic no-op audits, restores or preserves the prior ledger bytes, and proves `git diff --exit-code -- choices.json choices.md` is clean after a no-op re-audit.
findings.resolution: Revise F2 and task 3.6 so commit policy matches the existing volatile header behavior, or add a scoped task that makes no-op audit output byte-stable without changing the ledger schema.

findings.summary: The range scenario is not actually covered by the planned test
findings.description: Critical: Scenario 11 is about invoking the audit with an explicit `<base-sha>..<head-sha>` range and no change directory, but task 3.6 only says to assert the ledger records `change_id == "range:<base>..<head>"` and exits 0. That can be satisfied by calling `run_audit.py` with a precomputed synthetic change id, bypassing the standalone range argument resolution the requirement names.
findings.recommendation: Update task 3.6 to exercise the actual `/audit-choices <base>..<head>` resolution path, or add a small tested range-resolver entry point under `skills/audit-choices/scripts/` and have both the skill text and test use it.
findings.resolution: Make the test fail if `<base>..<head>` parsing is broken, rather than only checking that `run_audit.py` can persist a caller-supplied `range:` change id.
